findings.caveat: NOT a drop-in rename: the replacement returns a STRONG reference (Py_XNewRef) where this returns a BORROWED one, so a bare rename leaks the referent at every call site. Correct migration is rename + a matching Py_DECREF once the value is no longer needed. No-frame behaviour is identical (both return NULL without setting an exception), so the NULL guard needs no change.
findings.detail: PyEval_GetBuiltins is deprecated since 3.13. The named replacement is PyEval_GetFrameBuiltins, but it is NOT a drop-in. CAVEAT: NOT a drop-in rename: the replacement returns a STRONG reference (Py_XNewRef) where this returns a BORROWED one, so a bare rename leaks the referent at every call site. Correct migration is rename + a matching Py_DECREF once the value is no longer needed. No-frame behaviour is identical (both return NULL without setting an exception), so the NULL guard needs no change. (Doc/c-api/reflection.rst:10 (PEP 667). Returns a borrowed reference.)

_PyObject_GC_UNTRACK in tp_dealloc 'dictiter_dealloc', but the constructor 'dictiter_new' frees the object at line 5646 before _PyObject_GC_TRACK runs (linked via name prefix). On that error path dealloc gets an untracked object and the macro's _PyObject_ASSERT_FROM(op, _PyObject_GC_IS_TRACKED(op)) aborts -- a recoverable allocation failure becomes a SIGABRT. Use the untracked-tolerant PyObject_GC_UnTrack here. (It is tolerant of the untracked *state*, not of a NULL pointer: _PyObject_GC_IS_TRACKED still dereferences unconditionally.)
PyMem_NEW is deprecated since 2.0. Use PyMem_New instead (drop-in). (Doc/c-api/memory.rst:304. 26 real call sites.)
